structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E034. Tip is E034: 5.481 s, 0.7539 on seeds 0-2 (freeze of group 1 and whitening bias at 75% of steps, 9.25 epochs, 231 steps, batch 2000, 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%, wd x0.5). The held-out mean is unknown to me. The E027 base sat at about 0.7526, so the real margin over 0.753 is about zero.

Mechanisms, each tied to measured runs:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.2 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 confirms freeze plus +0.5 epoch nets -0.40 s vs E027 at +0.0 pp on seeds 0-2. That is better than my prediction, since the freeze saved more than the epochs cost.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, E006, confounded) are in the tip. Averaging and optimizer settings look tuned. A harder pull (E025), a longer interval (E030) and late LS=0 (E032) all hurt. wd, LS, Muon lr, LR floor and warm-up are flat within noise. Time-neutral boosters have failed 5 times in a row.
3. Time tracks pixels and FLOPs, sublinearly on small maps. Early low-res is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28 px and 32 px phases carry the accuracy (E018, E024).
4. Backward truncation is the best lever found. E028 saved 0.5 s, and the memory-bound group-1 maps explain why it saves more than its MAC share. It cost about 0.35 pp alone, but the stack with epochs recovers that. Selecting examples (E031) is worse.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Held-out sits about 0.2 pp below seeds 0-2. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I overpredicted time on trims and freezes (savings run 2-8% larger than modelled). I was too optimistic on time-neutral accuracy changes. I underestimated how well the freeze stacks with epochs.

Unsure: the held-out margin of E034. It may sit at about 0.752, so the bar is at risk. Systems-only changes (prepare cleanup, E033-style) are safe and small, about 0.05-0.1 s. Extra freeze dose probably costs accuracy at about the epoch-dial rate.

forecasts.reason: Bit-identical math, so accuracy is the same. It saves about 0.06 s from trial-0 warmup and the uint8 transfer.
The whitening bias is likely already stopped at 3 epochs, which is about 32% of steps. Stopping it at 20% saves a little backward work. The gain is small and the RNG re-roll adds noise.
Moving the freeze from 75% to 60% of steps saves about 0.2 s and costs about 0.15-0.3 pp. That is roughly the epoch-dial rate.
This is a diagnostic with no recipe change. I expect fresh seeds to land near the held-out mean of about 0.752, with a pooled mean near the bar.
Folding BN into the conv in the frozen phase removes some memory traffic. It also adds complexity and eval-mode mismatch risk. The gain is modest.
The profile will most likely show non-GEMM kernels and group 1 taking a large share of a 32 px step. I expect it to support H6.3.1.
Replacing Muon with SGD should lose about 0.3-0.5 pp. It saves a little time from dropping Newton-Schulz.

cruxes: What is E034's held-out seeds 3-12 mean? If it is below 0.752, the tip is not safe and an accuracy booster outranks any time cut.
How much of the 5.48 s is fixed cost (prepare, trial-0 warmup, eval-independent overhead)? If it is above 0.25 s, the systems cleanup is the cheapest remaining gain.
Is the whitening bias already stopped early in the code? If it is, I054 is a no-op.
